newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close higher on last-minute buying.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close higher on last-minute buying.

text.p: Philippine shares recovered slightly at close on late-session buying after drifting in the negative territory through most of the session, brokers said.
"There was late buying on selected big-cap issues ... Hong Kong was not in the game, so a lot of investors were inactive," Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities Phils Inc, said.
The composite index ended 6.33 points up at 2,815.54 after sliding to its intra-day low of 2,786.09.
Turnover was measly at 1.5 billion pesos against Monday's 1.99 billion.
In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 62 to 47, but all indices were firmer except for the commercial-industrial index.
San Miguel Corp faced follow-through selling for most of the session on concerns over its earnings following a price cut in its beer products.
However, San Miguel A rebounded and closed unchanged at 43 pesos while B shares, which are open to foreigners, ended two pesos down at 67.50 pesos.
"I think the market will continue to consolidate due to lack of liquidity as the market in Hong Kong is still close," Henry Ong, analyst at Sapphire Securities, said.
"I see no bright spot yet. There are no major news and corporate earnings for the second quarter may not be exciting," David de la Cruz, vice-president for marketing at Amsteel Securities, said.
Traders have pegged the near-term support at 2,750 points.
